I've always wanted a Stardew Valley-like game where I don't have to control a character. I want it automated and this is that game.

In Rusty’s Retirement, everything moves at a slow, predictable pace.
Fields grow on their own. Machines follow fixed paths.
All I have to do is stay nearby and let time pass naturally.

I really like its fully automated design.
Harvesting, watering, maintenance—none of it requires repeated input.
Rusty walks back and forth across the farm, quietly completing tasks that would normally demand my attention.
The little robot isn’t clever, but it’s reliable.
It moves one tile at a time—step, turn, pause, continue—
as if maintaining order in its own simple way.
Watching it work brings a surprising sense of calm:
things are being taken care of, and I don’t have to be drained by them.

The crops follow their own rhythm, which makes the game perfect to keep running while I focus.
I leave it on while writing papers, organizing materials, or working through complex problems.

Ridiculously cute idle game. A bit micro-managey at the beginning, but prioritizing the buildings that help with automation (Echo for upgrading bots and Splunk for automatic seed planting) makes letting the farm idle much easier and spending time decorating or redecorating more enjoyable. I love watching my little robots working on their farm on my extra monitor while I'm working on my others (I have three screens and this is perfect!). :)

I think the part I enjoyed most (aside from the achievements) is that it has replayability and multiple types of farms you can unlock, each with their own individual challenges.

I also love the stickers in the points shop for this one! They are super cute and I'll be saving up to get all of them.  <3

For more reviews and recommendations check out the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45071674-Under-Starry-Skies/] Under Starry Skies [/url]

"A relaxing idle-farming simulator that sits at the bottom of your screen while you do other things"

Can anyone actually focus on doing other things while this game takes up a third of the screen, makes noises, and things keep moving in it? Or am I just too easy to distract?

Dangerous ADHD trap game that's hard to leave alone.... 
Just kidding. 
But seriously, I often found myself just staring at this in the corner of my screen instead of letting it manage itself. Something kind of fun to play with on the side of your screen while doing something else. 

Not super intrusive. Can run along the bottom of your screen or along the side. It's kind of like a desktop widget but bigger.

Anyways, this is perfect for someone who intentionally wants to get distracted doing their work or something.

Took ~146 hours to 100%. (Left running unsupervised, not actively playing)

[u]Rusty's Retirement[/u] is the one that pioneered the bottom-of-your-screen game genre. It describes itself as an idle-farming sim, a game that doesn't demand your constant focus and attention. In other words, it's meant for multitasking. Let it run on the background while you work or browse.

I'd say that this demands more attention than what I expect from idlers. When you've just started, the seeds don't plant themselves unless you do, and there will be no additional help until you unlock a character (Splunk) that does it occasionally. In addition, early game crops without the upgrades means you're going to replant seeds more frequently.

I know it will make the game fully idle but I wish that besides Splunk, there are bots that can replant the seeds automatically. Splunk can't do it alone efficiently, at least if you're like me who have unlocked all the plots in one farm and filled

Pretty good. Easy to learn and play and generally satisfactory gameplay.

There's no progression to keep between new farms and I guess that's intentional, but I'd at least let you keep chips since they don't feel very impactful and you'd get more use out of some cool early-crop chips.

The berry bush / bees thing feels undercooked since it's just another way to get biofuel and berry bushes are the same just taking longer for more fuel.

I'm only 3 hours in, currently, but this is exactly what I wanted from something that you run while doing something else. 

Some of these types of games have just a little too much going on, where you find yourself spending more time than you really were supposed to on the game. For something that's meant to sort of idle as a "multi-tasking" sort of thing, that means you're not really multi-tasking. The games are fun, of course, but you're no longer doing what you intended, which was a balance of doing the thing you're struggling to do- the productivity- and the game, which is too fun to ignore. 

Rusty's Retirement kind of nailed that down. 

I WANT to focus on the game, but it takes time. It has to work through the things it's doing, so I have nothing to do but be productive while it does its thing. Eventually, I hit this really nice flow state where I can occasionally sit back,

[h1]Short Review[/h1]
Rusty's Retirement is the perfect mix of active and idle content for a desktop companion game. It's an idle-farming sim that sits at the bottom of your screen, but there's actually a ton to engage with beyond just watching numbers go up. I'm not a fan of desktop idlers that don't have much substance to them, and this definitely isn't one of those. Between the layout optimization, the wonderful pixel art, and the way the game politely gets out of your way when you need it to, this one's a very easy recommendation.

[h1]Full Review[/h1]
Rusty's Retirement has you growing crops, producing biofuel, and deploying a team of little robots to automate your farm, all while the whole thing sits at the bottom of your screen so you can work or browse on top of it. Coming from other desktop idlers, I was cautiously optimistic going in, but this one ended up being one of the bett
this game saved my mother from a burning building and fixed my credit, you should totally buy it.
New genre creator, bottom of your screen games motivate you to do something you'd procrastinate, definitely a must-have game

Such a chill game to throw onto the other monitor while watching smth, playing a game, studying, etc. Atm I only have about 40 hrs so I'm not "done" with the game yet this game has a lot to offer. If you just want a chill idle farming game to put to the side while doing stuff I'd recommend. My only complaint is that sometimes it needs more attention then other idle games and it takes up a good bit of your screen that's why putting it on the other monitor helps. Other than that fantastic game 8.5/10

A wonderful little game to keep you company while watching videos or even while playing another game with friends. Took me 128 hours to get all the achievements but the time flew by like nothing highly recommend. Positives are the art the gameplay the easy controls the negatives are uhhhhhhh idk I never experienced anything negative in my time so I couldn't say.
This game heals the soul.  Amazing while drawing or doing office work at the computer.  The music helps you focus and forget outside worries.  I love helping rusty tend to the land!  Amazing game!

Not much of a farming sim person but this is a nice way to tame my easily distracted brain while working. Yes it still is technically a distraction from work, but it keeps me in the right set of windows to keep things going.

Possibly my favorite little desktop aid. It does wonders for my ability to pay attention during calls, or when working. When my ADHD redirects my attention it can just focus on a little bit of farming without tabbing out or losing my place in whatever work I was doing. LOVE it!

Fun idler - though its largely hands on. I wish progress carried between farms, mostly just the money and bio crystals and plant unlocks would be nice. There are frustrations when it comes to placement, as well as things you simply cannot destroy once placed.

One of the most iconic bottom-of-your-screen idle games I've ever played. So chill, so nice! You get to see Rusty do his own thing and occasionally help him tend his farm/ranch more efficiently. Simple controls, good progression, cute pixel art style, but for me the UI can still be improved for easier building/upgrading/removing. A must-buy for those who like a chill companion enjoy his retirement while you work and/or play your ass off, haha.

Rusty’s Retirement is a really cute concept for an idle game. It sits at the bottom of your screen while you do other things, slowly farming away in the background. It’s relaxing and low-pressure, and I genuinely enjoyed having it running while I worked or browsed.

That said, it’s not quite the perfect idle experience. The “idle” mechanics don’t always work as smoothly as I’d hoped, and you can’t upgrade certain parts of the process — only the bots. Once you pick a farm layout, you’re locked in, and buildings or animals can’t be removed after placing them, which feels surprisingly restrictive. On top of that, several achievements require starting completely new saves multiple times, which can feel a bit tedious.

Even with those frustrations, I still had a good time and ended up 100% completing it. It’s charming, cozy, and satisfying in its own way — just not my favorite idle game o

I love checking the game every hour and seeing Rusty just minding his own business — watering and harvesting crops. Having bots and friends helping around the farm is such a delight to see. There are also different biomes for your farm, but I still like the default one the best!
To work in the game industry I only have time to play idle games while coding and LeetCoding. While it is what it is, this one is comforting.

Once you choose a farm layout, you can't change it.
Once you place animals, you can't remove them.
5+ achievements require you to make multiple saves, starting from the beginning multiple times.
Gets repetitive extremely fast, not very fun and requires a lot more attention than an afk game should

Less of a game and more of interactive wall paper.  If you go into this looking for an idle game this really isn't much of a game.  IF you go into this trying to optimize production structures there really isn't that type of game.  And to my knowledge there isn't an endgame or goal.  

Basically treat it like background music and something to occasionally look at and its kind of interesting.  If you're looking for an actual game I'd look else where.

It's a bit too involved for a lot of the game for my idle game tastes. You can't fully automate until you unlock the final resident. Up until that point you need to manually plant at fairly frequent intervals since crops get picked pretty quickly. The game is also a bit too big on the screen to just let it run in front of any other window.
It seems like it can be fun. However the layout of this game is aggravating. Without a windowed mode I can not recommend this.

It is actually bonkers to me that there is no full screen option, literally, why? Every screenshot of this game is a zoomed in one. Dual monitors exist; there is no reason in this day and age not to have full screen as an option. Being able to play it while doing stuff is sick, but that being the entire focus and forgetting that some people may want to focus entirely on the game is wild. So many issues arise, like people with bad vision struggling to play this game simply because everything is too tiny to see. The zoom in features only go to 1/4 of the screen and change almost nothing. The base font in this game is also really hard on the eyes and a wild choice for how tiny the game window is. However, there is an alternative font option that is much appreciated.
Looks like a nice enough game but it does not work properly on Linux (runs on a black window, no overlay possible, kinda defeats the concept...). Would have preferred to know that before buying.

I just lost nearly 3 hours of progress. Even though the game is supposed to have an autosave feature, it failed to work, and my save file has reverted to the first 5 minutes of play. I can't find my recent data anywhere.

Not a true idler game. It cannot just sit alone and do its thing while you do other things. You have to keep an eye on the game and plant crops, where you make active decisions in the game. 

Better just buy Ropuka's Island folks. In that game, Ropuka cuts the grass, and you doing anything beyond just opening the game and letting him loose is optional.
A sad follow up to Haiku the robot. I don't really understand the point of the game. Not for me.

I shouldn't really be reviewing this, since I don't really play idle games much, and this was not made for me. I just like reviewing games I played to remember my thoughts. My review doesn't count toward the overall score anyways, since I didn't buy it on steam.

Anyway, it's an idle game, for ants. Like, you just get this small bar at the bottom(or side) of your screen with a very small UI. Maybe this a dream for idle game players with just one monitor, but it made it difficult for me to play. I found a zoom in function, but the ramp up was too slow for me to want to continue. It seems if you zoom in you can't see part of the game anyways, but it probably moves I'm guessing if needed.

I don't know, I probably spent more time writing this reivew than playing this game. You might like it if you really like idle games, and want to multitask. Not for me though.

Can't recommend at the current price. You get a little fun from this game. The art is cute, and the growth is satisfying, but if you are halfway competent or just leave the game on for a while, you will easily unlock everything in a single sitting and be left with little to do other than unlock all the plants you can plant. This left me feeling like I had nothing left to work for and all the new upgrades felt hollow because of it. 

I could make more money, but what was there left to buy?

(also its a bit of a cpu hog, had trouble running other games or expensive programs while it was up.)

Linux and Steam Deck users beware:
- requires special Wine/Proton configuration to enable windowed mode. (Check the pinned discussions in the game's discussion forum)
- the transparency this game uses to render correctly on your desktop is broken under Wine/Proton.

I don't know about others, but this wasn't fun for me. I tried to just play the game, and it wasn't fun. I also tried it while working or watching videos, etc., but it still wasn't fun. I didn't like the progression system  and gameplay wasnt that interesting. It looks like I am not a fan of bottom-of-the-screen type games. I would rather put an idle game on my second monitor than this.

Not what I was looking for. More of a screensaver rather than a game. It takes a small portion of the screen so you can watch it while doing other things. Its "game" elements are very limited and contains no offline progression (not that it needs it). 

Pros: Bug free. 
Cons: CPU usage. Even considering it more as a "screen saver" rather than an actual game, I can not recommend it. It uses a considerable amount of CPU, 6-16% depending on the graphics settings.

Not really an idle game until you spend enough time grinding to unlock the guy who might plant things for you, meaning you have to come back consistently to plant things for this game to do anything. Sure, it has the slow progression of most idlers, but requiring the 'player' to constantly return and interact with the game for anything to happen makes it less of an idler, and reminds me more of the old facebook-style farming games with long timers. 

Only good if you're working on the computer, and on things you don't mind interrupting every minute or few to plant seeds so Rusty and his bot buddies have something to do. As I was hoping for something I could leave running and return to have a look whenever I'm bored (you know, an idle game, like this one claims to be), I'm giving this a Not Recommended.

NOT RECOMMENDED due to this ONE problem

Problem

Hovering over the "Bulldoze" icon and the "moving pieces" icon doesn't tell you what they actually do. Ended up deleting one of my buildings(biofuel converter) thinking i was moving it, instead it was deleted permanently with NO way to get back or resources given back. And the way the game is, the buildings get even more expensive as you purchase them, so losing that ONE is still a HUGE loss.

Solution

Make it so when you hover over those specific icons, it'll tell you what they do. And if you "accidentally" delete a building you can recover them in a different "recycled or deleted" pieces OR refund them for half the price of what you bought it with. Just something so you don't COMPLETELY lose it.

Honestly just suffers from lack of catered progression because of the idle format. The replanting of seeds and general tediousness of each action becomes more apparent once you get past a certain point - and then it just becomes extremely annoying replanting and there's not much to do except watch your number go up (which happens when youre not even playing - so the progression gets messed up)
Rusty, I want to love you, you seem like a perfectly nice robot, but please, PLEASE, stop putting wheat in the biofuel generator. I have so many other crops you could use!

This is a sorry excuse for an idler game. Too much of my play through, I had to do something about every 4-12 minutes. The 12m being on a market that shows up to upgrade plants.
